top.title: Red Sox's Triston Casas Hits Home Run In First At-Bat In 574 Days
top.description: Boston Red Sox first baseman Triston Casas The Major League Baseball Season may be over, but baseball is still happening around the world. The Dominican Winter League is one of the premier winter leagues, and this year, Triston Casas is playing for the Tigres Del Licey. On Friday night, he played in his first game of the season and hit a grand slam in the bottom of the first inning. TRISTON CASAS GRAND SLAM IN HIS FIRST LIDOM PA SINCE OCT 2022 pic.twitter.com/tNNrDspcHB — Sarah Langs (@SlangsOnSports) November 28, 2026 It was Casas' first at-bat in any league since May 2, 2025, 574 days ago. This is Casas' second time suiting up for the Tigres Del Licey. The first stint he had in the Dominican Winter League came in 2022. His grand slam was his lone hit of the game, but it is a potential sign of what's to come when he's back in the big leagues. Casas was great in the only big league season in which he played over 130 games. In 2023, he slashed .263/.367/.490 with 24 home runs. However, he has battled injuries ever since. In 2024, he missed 99 games with torn cartilage in his rib cage, but still hit 13 home runs with a .800 OPS in 63 games. In 2025, he got off to a slow start and then ruptured his left patellar tendon. He missed the rest of the year, suffered setbacks this year, and missed all of the 2026 season. This year, he dealt with an abdominal strain and underwent wrist surgery. Things are different now for the Red Sox than they were the last time Casas played. They have a new starting first baseman, and with Jake Bauers also on the team, Casas may not even be the backup. At-bats will be hard to come by for him, and he could be traded. top.title: Kentucky basketball’s illegal in-bounds play has fans creating Mark Pope replacement lists
top.description: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mark Pope entered the year with Kentucky men’s basketball desperately needing a signature season and a deep NCAA tournament run to save his job and regain the momentum of the program. Instead, Pope’s Wildcats are already in danger of missing March Madness less than a month into the 2026-27 campaign after suffering their third embarrassing loss so far on Friday night. Wichita State beat Kentucky, 73-71 in overtime, on a loss that can be blamed directly on coaching. Kentucky already got destroyed by Kansas in the Champions Classic, then lost handily to a good-not-great Indiana team. This Wichita State loss feels like the new low point of the Pope era, not because the Shockers are bad — they’re now ranked nine spots ahead of Kentucky on KenPom — but because of how the Wildcats lost. Pope was booed off the floor at home as he walked off the court after the loss to Wichita State. He deserved it for how poorly he managed the end of the game. Kentucky should have had one last chance to tie or win the game down two with 5.4 seconds remaining in overtime. Pope went into the huddle and drew up a play that directly resulted in a turnover. The Wildcats tried to get tricky inbounding the ball under their own basket, but Pope’s play was illegal for passing the ball across the baseline. This is as humiliating as it gets for a coach already under fire. Kentucky inbound turnover pic.twitter.com/ryIWoB4QPo — wok (@wokdior) November 28, 2026 Pope took full accountability for the play after the game. “That’s 100% on me, guys. That is 100% me. Somehow that changed to a live ball in my mind and I messed that up. And it’s really costly. It’s a tough one to carry as a coach, for sure. Kentucky’s final play wasn’t their only miscue. Down two with 35 seconds left, Pope drew up a play for his $6 million man Milan Momcilovic , who promptly stepped out of bounds. Watch the play here: Milan Momcilovic steps out of bounds wow pic.twitter.com/SjqzMju5dN — wok (@wokdior) November 28, 2026 Kentucky actually did get one more chance to win the game after the illegal play on the baseline. Wichita State turned the ball over on the next possession, and Momcilovic got a decent look at a game-winning three, but missed. What this comes down to is poor execution by Kentucky, and it has Big Blue Nation ready to move on. Pope heard some boos from the home fans as he walked off the floor after the game: Mark Pope Boo’d out of Rupp Arena pic.twitter.com/C4n2tEvQ0z — Bleed Blue Network (@BleedBNetwork) November 28, 2026 Kentucky fell to No. 66 on KenPom after the loss . top.title: Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in final practice for F1 Qatar GP
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian Formula One driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes drives during the second practice of the Formula 1 2026 Qatar Grand Prix, at Lusail International Circuit. (is associated with: «Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in final practice for F1 Qatar GP») Alessio Morgese/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa World champion Kimi Antonelli led a third Mercedes one-two ahead of team-mate George Russell in the final practice for the Formula One Qatar Grand Prix on Saturday. The top two was a repetition of the previous two practice sessions on Friday. The Italian clocked the fastest time of 1 minute 22.400 seconds, beating Russell by 0.249 seconds. Max Verstappen of Red Bull was third ahead of team-mate Isack Hadjar. Charles Leclerc of Ferrari was fifth, with the McLaren duo of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri right behind in sixth and seventh respectively. Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton was ninth in the other Ferrari. The race in Qatar is taking place despite continuing security concerns due to conflicts in the Middle East. Several broadcasters and other personnel decided against attending the penultimate race of the season. Williams driver Carlos Sainz, who was 18th in practice, revealed on Thursday that drivers were briefed on emergency evacuation procedures and was surprised to discover journalists knew nothing about it. "I was told there was such a plan, and I expected the press would be included, too," he said. Qualifying for Sunday's showdown is later on Saturday. There's nothing more at stake at this point of the year, as Antonelli has already clinched the drivers' title and Mercedes have claimed the constructors' championship.

top.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, organised mocked polls across the country today with mixed results and turnouts. The exercise was to test INEC’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, expecially the technical aspects. However, despite reports of poor numbers, the INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, expressed satisfaction with the conduct of the nationwide mock accreditation exercise. He assured Nigerians of the commission’s readiness to deliver credible elections in 2027. Amupitan, who visited Jos on Saturday to monitor the exercise, inspected polling locations, including Obasanjo Model School in Jos South Local Government Area, where he observed voter accreditation and the performance of electoral technology. Speaking to journalists, the INEC chairman described the turnout and conduct of the exercise as impressive. “You can see yourself that it is very impressive. The turnout is very good,” he said. Uploaded results Meanwhile, about 1,995 results (approximately 12%) of the 17,614 expected, had been uploaded as of 3:09 pm on Saturday in the nationwide INEC mock presidential election. The Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise, which started at 8:30a.m., ended at 2:30pm. However, more than 30 minutes later, the portal puts the “Percentage uploaded” at 11.33 per cent. Its last recorded upload came at 3:09:11 pm from polling unit 32/04/05/005, at press time. Low turnout in Lagos Low turnout of eligible voters marred the mock accreditation exercise conducted in parts of Lagos State, with some voters blaming the commission’s inadequate publicity. Polling agents expressed concern over the poor participation when Vanguard visited some of the designated polling units in Ijegun, Satellite Town and Festac, in the Amuwo-Odofin area of the state. An INEC polling agent at one of the polling units said only about 40 of the 250 registered voters had participated in the exercise as of the time of the visit. …in Katsina, too; poor publicity Also, low voter turnout and inadequate public awareness characterised the mock accreditation exercise conducted by lNEC in Katsina State on Saturday, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The low participation raised concerns about the level of public sensitisation and awareness among eligible voters regarding the importance of the exercise. top.description: Nations Championship Wales (26) 40 Tries: Adams 2, Murray, Morgan-Williams, Morgan 2 Cons: Costelow 5 Japan (0) 10 Tries: Komura, Vailea Wales finished their Nations Championship campaign with another victory against Japan in a six-try display at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. Wing Josh Adams and replacement flanker Jac Morgan claimed two tries apiece, with full-back Blair Murray and scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams also dotting down, while player of the match Sam Costelow kicked 10 points. This set up the most comprehensive margin of victory of the Steve Tandy coaching era in a match that was affected by the miserable conditions. Despite the scoreline, Wales again spent large periods of the game defending against a weakened Japan side who managed two late tries through replacements Shinya Komura and Halatoa Vailea. Returning flanker James Botham made 38 tackles as he equalled Dafydd Jenkins' world record effort in the 35-28 win against New Zealand, a mark they now both share with Thierry Dusautoir of France. It was a curious contest, low on quality, played in front of a half-empty Twickenham as part of a double-header before England faced New Zealand. The victory means Wales secured ninth in the inaugural Nations Championship and finished the year ninth in World Rugby's rankings. It was a second win in the space of three weeks against Japan, and a third victory in a November campaign that will forever be remembered for Wales beating New Zealand for the first time in 73 years. Wales struggle to create early energy Wales had unconvincingly defeated Japan 28-21 in the opening game of the November series, following up that with the famous win against the All Blacks before a narrow loss to Australia. Both Wales and Japan had finished fifth in their respective hemisphere sections to set up a fifth contest between Wales and Japan inside 17 months. Eddie Jones' side had suffered heavy 60-point defeats to England and Scotland and were down to the bare bones with flanker Tiennan Costley named on the wing. Wales initially made five changes with Morgan-Williams making his first Test start and prop Rhys Carre, hooker Ryan Elias, lock Adam Beard and Botham also included. With hooker Dewi Lake and Morgan dropping to the bench, lock Dafydd Jenkins captained the side for the first time in more than two years. There was another late alteration when wing Louis Rees-Zammit was ruled out because of illness, with Scarlets back Ellis Mee promoted from the bench for his first action of this November campaign. top.title: Bucks add games against Jazz and Raptors to schedule
top.description: Following the conclusion of preliminary NBA Cup play late on Nov. 27, the league added two regular-season games to the December schedule for teams that did not advance to the knockout rounds of the in-season tournament. The Milwaukee Bucks were one of those teams, and they had games against the Utah Jazz and Toronto Raptors added to their schedule. Milwaukee will head to Utah on Dec. 6 for a 4 p.m. CT game and host the Raptors on Dec. 10 at 7 p.m. CT. The Jazz game is an interesting addition, as the Bucks already had a trip to Salt Lake City on their schedule Jan. 26 as part of a West Coast trip. The game against the Raptors also will be the team's fourth meeting of the season and second at Fiserv Forum. The teams already have played twice, including the Bucks' second win of the season on Nov. 23. top.title: Skip Bayless says Cowboys would’ve won vs Eagles if they had made the Dak Prescott trade he told them to
top.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images Skip Bayless has continued to express his displeasure for Dak Prescott on the back of the Dallas Cowboys losing to the Philadelphia Eagles. The Cowboys are now 5-7 for the season after giving up 21 points against the Eagles, meaning there is a strong chance they will now go three years in a row without reaching the postseason. But rather than questioning Dallas’ defence, which is the worst in the league right now, Bayless has instead spoken of his desire to trade Dak Prescott for Jayden Daniels. Skip Bayless thinks Jayden Daniels would have helped the Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles Bayless already commented on his desire to trade Prescott for Daniels prior to the November trade deadline. Speaking in late October, he said: “If they want to trade me Jayden Daniels for Dak Prescott. It’s done. Straight up, player for player. Let me have him, I’ll take it. He was available all last year when we went 7-9-1. He’s been available this year; we’re 2-4. Give me Jayden Daniels.” Now, on the latest episode of Gridiron, Bayless has once again been speaking about trading for Daniels and this time claimed that the quarterback ‘gets that game home’ [against the Eagles]. He said: “If there’s some way that Washington would trade me Jayden Daniels straight up for Dak Prescott, which they would laugh at, I would do it in a heartbeat because I’ve got 25 years old versus 33, and I’ve got the clutch gene versus no clutch gene. That’s just me.” His fellow host replied: “Yeah, and you still would have lost 38-39 yesterday,” seeing Skip respond by suggesting Daniels would have won them the game. He said: “No, I would not have. Jayden Daniels gets that game home. He’s going to just keep on keeping on in the fourth quarter. He’s going to throw two more touchdown passes in the fourth quarter.” While Skip seems keen to move on from Prescott, Daniels’ stats have not been that impressive this season. He has 1,788 passing yards (3,340 for Dak), 10 passing touchdowns versus 27 for the Cowboys star and has a completion rate of 64.9% compared to 65.8% for Prescott. Bayless also mentioned Daniels having a ‘clutch gene’, which may be the only area he actually has the better of the Dallas QB. Prescott is 2-5 in postseason games throughout his career, while the Washington Commanders star is 2-1. nigeria.title: Tinubu’s reforms push Nigeria’s foreign reserves to $54.13bn – City Boy Movement
nigeria.description: The City Boy Movement has hailed the rise in Nigeria’s gross foreign reserves to $54.13 billion, describing the development as evidence of progress under President Bola Tinubu’s economic reform agenda. The group said the reserves had reached their second-highest level on record since 1999, surpassed only by the $62.08 billion peak recorded in September 2008, when the global financial crisis was unfolding. In a statement titled, “Why Tinubu 4+4? Foreign Reserves Edition,” the movement said Nigeria’s foreign reserves had increased significantly under the Tinubu administration, rising from $32.29 billion in May 2023 to $54.13 billion in November 2026. It put the increase at $21.84 billion, representing nearly 68 per cent growth since the President assumed office. According to the group, the latest figures place Nigeria’s foreign reserves above the peak levels recorded in several years, including 2009, 2007, 2013, 2018, 2025, 2019, 2012 and 2014. The movement noted that Nigeria’s reserves peaked at $53.25 billion in 2009, $51.33 billion in 2007, $48.86 billion in 2013 and $47.87 billion in 2018. It added that the $54.13 billion recorded in 2026 represented the highest level since the 2008 global financial crisis. While acknowledging the difficulties associated with the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, the group argued that the latest reserve figures indicated that the policies were beginning to yield positive results. It said the growth in foreign reserves was an important development in assessing the direction of the economy, expressing optimism that the country was moving towards greater economic prosperity. “The significance is in the history. Even though the reforms have been difficult, the numbers are beginning to tell their own story. We are on the way to prosperity,” the statement said. The movement also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for what it described as progress in the management of the country’s external reserves, reaffirming its support for the President. The figures cited by the group were attributed to data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). However, the movement’s assessment comes amid continuing public debate over the impact of the Federal Government’s economic reforms, particularly their effects on inflation, living costs, businesses and household welfare. nigeria.description: By Chinedu Adonu The nationwide mock accreditation exercise recorded a poor turnout in most polling centres in Enugu State on Saturday, with as few as two voters accredited by the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) in some centres as of 12 noon. A correspondent who monitored the exercise observed that the low turnout could be attributed to poor public awareness, late arrival of Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ad hoc staff and difficulties encountered by some voters in locating their designated polling units. The exercise also coincided with the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Enugu State. At polling centres in Igbariam, Idaw River and Obiagu, among others, INEC ad hoc staff were observed arriving between 9:30 a.m. and 10 a.m., raising concerns about the late commencement of the exercise. Speaking at the Obiagu polling centre, a community leader, who identified himself simply as Mr Friday, attributed the poor turnout partly to the presidential visit. He said many residents had left their homes to receive President Tinubu at Okpara Square. According to him, those who turned out to welcome the President cut across party lines, as members of the APC and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), under the Rainbow Coalition, trooped out in large numbers. “So, it is clear that very few voters are currently around for the exercise, and most are not even aware or mobilised by local political leaders to participate,” he said. Also speaking, a resident of Achara Layout, Mr Arinze Madu, said he had visited two designated polling centres in search of his polling unit but had yet to locate his name. “There is little awareness to enable people know the designated polling units for the exercise in this Registration Area (RA), which is also a ward,” Madu said. nigeria.title: Apathy mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Abia
nigeria.description: …Voter alleges demand for N1m to participate By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Voter apathy marred the mock accreditation and result-upload exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Abia State on Saturday, with several polling units recording zero or minimal turnout. At Ibeku High School, one of the designated polling centres, Vanguard observed at about noon that no voter had turned up, while INEC officials waited for participants. A staff member of YIAGA Africa, who was monitoring the exercise, was also sighted at the centre but declined to comment. The situation was similar at School Road Primary School and Ugba Primary School, where electoral officials were on ground but voters were absent. Voters fault poor publicity, limited coverage At St. Stephen’s Primary School, Umuahia, however, some residents who turned out expressed disappointment that the exercise was restricted to selected polling units, blaming inadequate publicity for the low participation. Chimwe Kanu, a public servant, said she was excited about participating until she discovered that her polling unit was not among those selected for the exercise. “I’m happy to be here and to do the needful, but coming here, nothing is really happening because I was unable to vote or be captured. My polling unit is not part of the polling units selected. “I’m very disappointed because the happiness I came with, I didn’t see it again,” she said. Kanu said many prospective participants left after discovering that the exercise was limited to designated polling units. She urged INEC to improve its preparations for the 2027 general elections, particularly by ensuring the timely distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). “Many don’t have their voters’ cards. Their names are here, but their voters’ cards have not been given to them. They should make sure they share the voters’ cards as soon as possible. People need their voters’ cards,” she said. She also called on the commission to ensure early arrival of election officials and seamless accreditation of eligible voters, expressing hope that it would conduct credible elections in 2027. Similarly, Mike Uche criticised the publicity for the exercise, saying many residents arrived at polling centres unaware that participation was restricted to designated units. He said inadequate sensitisation left many confused and frustrated, alleging that some prospective participants demanded financial inducements before agreeing to take part in the exercise. Uche urged INEC to intensify voter education through radio announcements, community outreach and street sensitisation to improve participation and enlighten the electorate on the purpose of such exercises. “People are eager to come out and do the mock accreditation. nigeria.title: Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Katsina
nigeria.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina Low voter turnout and inadequate public awareness characterised the mock accreditation exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Katsina State on Saturday ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vanguard monitoring of the exercise at Star Election Polling Unit, Wakilin Kudu 1, Kofar Gidan Iro Isansi, Rafin Dadi, showed that only a few voters turned out to participate, although some were successfully accredited. The low participation raised concerns about the level of public sensitisation and awareness among eligible voters regarding the importance of the exercise. The mock accreditation exercise is designed to test the functionality of the accreditation system, assess the preparedness of electoral officials and identify possible technical and operational challenges ahead of the actual elections. At the polling unit, the participation of the few voters provided an opportunity to observe the practical application of the accreditation process and assess the readiness of electoral personnel. The development also highlighted the need for increased public enlightenment to ensure that eligible voters understand the purpose and significance of such exercises. Adequate sensitisation is considered essential to encouraging participation in mock exercises, which enable electoral authorities to test arrangements and address possible challenges before the main elections. The exercise also provides an opportunity to identify operational gaps and resolve potential difficulties that could affect the smooth conduct of the 2027 general elections. INEC is expected to strengthen public enlightenment and stakeholder engagement to improve awareness and encourage greater voter participation in subsequent electoral exercises. nigeria.title: Dangote Refinery set to list on NGX December 1
nigeria.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals FZE is scheduled to list 125,458,915,901 ordinary shares at N525 per share on the Main Board of Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday, 1 December 2026. The listing is expected to add approximately N65.87 trillion to the market capitalisation of NGX. The listing follows the company’s Initial Public Offering (IPO), which attracted approximately 3.8 million subscribers from 121 countries, including all 54 African countries, reflecting unprecedented investor participation in a Nigerian public equity offering. With a minimum subscription of N5,250 for 10 ordinary shares, the offer enabled investors across income groups and geographical locations to participate in the ownership of one of Africa’s largest industrial enterprises. Speaking at the launch of the IPO in September, Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, described the offer as an opportunity to broaden public ownership and enable more Nigerians and Africans to participate in industrial wealth creation. “The Dangote refinery IPO is more than an investment opportunity; it is an opportunity for millions of Nigerians and Africans to build lasting wealth through ownership of a world-class industrial asset,” Dangote said. Investor participation at this scale was facilitated by NGX Invest, the SEC-approved digital capital-raising platform launched by Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) in June 2024. By enabling a network of 186 distribution channels, including stockbrokers, banks, fintech platforms and WhatsApp, NGX Invest provided the rail that significantly broadened access to the public offer. Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, said: “The listing of Dangote Petroleum Refinery will mark an important milestone for Nigeria’s capital market, demonstrating its capacity to support large-scale industrial enterprises and mobilise long-term capital. The breadth of investor participation in the public offer also reflects the progress we have made in expanding market access. Through technology, strategic partnerships and a diverse distribution network, we are connecting more people to investment opportunities and more businesses to capital.” According to the company’s prospectus, net proceeds from the IPO will partly finance an estimated US$14.3 billion expansion programme designed to double refining capacity from 700,000 to approximately 1.4 million barrels per day. The transaction underscores the capital market’s strategic role in financing industrial expansion, broadening economic participation and supporting Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a US$1 trillion economy. Government officials, regulators, business leaders, market operators and representatives of African exchanges are expected to attend the listing ceremony. nigeria.title: INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan
nigeria.description: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission, in collaboration with security agencies, is taking necessary steps to address all security concerns ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​⁠‌‌‍‍‌‌​stated this on Saturday in Jos while speaking with newsmen during the monitoring of the ongoing mock accreditation. Addressing a question on the security challenge and the likely implications on voter participation, Amupitan said the safety of ad hoc staff and all Nigerians remained a priority to the commission. “As the chairman of INEC, I’m also worried about the state of security in Nigeria, but you can see we are taking some good steps to ensure that we nip it in the bud. “Just two days ago, we had a national security conference where we brought together all the members of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), the police, the military, the Civil Defence, and other paramilitary agencies. “So, we had a one-day conference where we discussed all these issues,” he said. Amupitan said that INEC had conducted a risk assessment of every part of Nigeria, using Election Risk Management (ERM) tools. “We have identified all the polling units that are vulnerable, and we have shared this with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extraordinary preparation for those places. “Any polling unit 500 meters from those vulnerable areas has been identified, and we are going to deal with it,” he said. Amupitan said the commission was interested in the security of the voters and ad hoc staff, particularly corps members. “It’s not every security matter you can bring to the open, but we are doing everything, both intelligence and physical, to ensure that the security on election day is assured,” he said. nigeria.title: 2027: Adebayo pledges poverty-free Nigeria, justice, security
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prince Adewole Adebayo, has promised to tackle poverty, insecurity, unemployment and other socio-economic challenges confronting Nigeria if elected in the 2027 general election. He also pledged to prioritise justice, free and quality education, affordable living costs and improved welfare for Nigerians. Adebayo spoke during a visit to the Emir of Lafia, His Royal Highness, Justice Sidi Dauda Bage Muhammad I (Rtd.), in Nasarawa State, where he presented the SDP’s vision and sought the monarch’s blessings ahead of the 2027 elections. The presidential candidate, who was accompanied by the SDP governorship candidate in Nasarawa State and former Inspector-General of Police, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, described the visit as particularly significant, noting that his relationship with the monarch went beyond politics. He said: “I am exceptionally happy today that, in all our appearances in this palace, this is the happiest because we came here with your son, IGP Abubakar Adamu.” Describing the Emir as a father, mentor and pillar of justice, Adebayo recalled his longstanding relationship with the monarch, dating back to his early years as a legal practitioner. He explained that the Emir had maintained a close relationship with his late uncle, who was the monarch’s friend during their days at law school. “His Highness is an uncle to me because he replaced my late uncle, who had been his friend since they were together in law school,” he said. Adebayo also recalled his professional encounters with Justice Bage, saying the monarch helped shape his understanding of courtroom practice when he appeared before him as a young lawyer. He recounted an incident during his first appearance before the monarch, when he was using what he described as his own style of English in court. “In my first appearance before His Lordship, I was appearing before Prince Adetokunbo Kayode, SAN. It was a very testy case, and I was using the language of my own English. His Lordship said, ‘We have our own language in this court.’ That is the language I have been using since that time,” he said. On the SDP’s choice of Adamu as its governorship candidate in Nasarawa, Adebayo described the former police chief as a distinguished professional whose experience in national and international policing would be valuable in addressing the state’s security challenges. He noted that Adamu’s service as a former Inspector-General of Police and Deputy Head of INTERPOL had strengthened the party’s confidence in his leadership capacity. “With Abubakar Adamu with us, we do not need to campaign because he is a professional of the highest distinction. He rose to the highest rank in the Nigerian Police and attained a high position in international policing as Deputy Head of INTERPOL,” he said. nigeria.title: Referee faces suspension after punching goalkeeper in post-match rawl
nigeria.description: A Bolivian referee, Jordy Aleman, might face be faced with strict suspension rules after punching Real Potosi goalkeeper Cristian Martinez during a post-match confrontation following the 2026 Copa Bolivia final. The incident occurred on Wednesday after Always Ready secured the trophy with a 3-1 aggregate victory over Real Potosi. The second leg ended in a goalless draw at the Victor Agustin Ugarte Stadium in Potosi. Tensions flared after the final whistle as Real Potosi players approached Aleman to protest decisions made during the match. Television footage showed the referee punching Martinez in the face, triggering further disorder before police intervened to protect the officials. Reports from Spanish-language media, including MARCA, said the confrontation followed an insult directed at Aleman by the goalkeeper. Martinez reportedly told the referee, “I hope your mother dies.” Martinez later said the punch left his mouth bleeding. However, in a defiant response reported by El Diario, he remarked: “He should hit harder.” The goalkeeper also questioned Aleman’s professionalism and called for an exemplary punishment. He subsequently announced that he would not pursue legal action or file a formal complaint over the incident. In a statement shared by Spanish publication 20 Minutos, Martinez said: “My intention is to consider this episode over and avoid allowing this situation to continue generating conflict.” Aleman could face disciplinary sanctions under the Bolivian Football Federation’s Disciplinary Code, which reportedly provides for fines of at least 20 national minimum monthly salaries and bans of between one and three years for physical assaults. The incident also led to four Real Potosi players and three members of the club’s coaching staff reportedly receiving red cards. According to Bolivian publication Vision 360, the federation’s refereeing authorities are expected to review the incident alongside the match reports. Aleman’s status as an international referee could also have further implications. The referee has yet to make a public statement on the incident. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). Instead, Pope’s Wildcats are already in danger of missing March Madness less than a month into the 2026-27 campaign after suffering their third embarrassing loss so far on Friday night. Wichita State beat Kentucky, 73-71 in overtime, on a loss that can be blamed directly on coaching. Kentucky already got destroyed by Kansas in the Champions Classic, then lost handily to a good-not-great Indiana team. This Wichita State loss feels like the new low point of the Pope era, not because the Shockers are bad — they’re now ranked nine spots ahead of Kentucky on KenPom — but because of how the Wildcats lost. Pope was booed off the floor at home as he walked off the court after the loss to Wichita State. He deserved it for how poorly he managed the end of the game. Kentucky should have had one last chance to tie or win the game down two with 5.4 seconds remaining in overtime. Pope went into the huddle and drew up a play that directly resulted in a turnover. The Wildcats tried to get tricky inbounding the ball under their own basket, but Pope’s play was illegal for passing the ball across the baseline. This is as humiliating as it gets for a coach already under fire. Kentucky inbound turnover pic.twitter.com/ryIWoB4QPo — wok (@wokdior) November 28, 2026 Pope took full accountability for the play after the game. “That’s 100% on me, guys. That is 100% me. Somehow that changed to a live ball in my mind and I messed that up. And it’s really costly. It’s a tough one to carry as a coach, for sure. Kentucky’s final play wasn’t their only miscue. Down two with 35 seconds left, Pope drew up a play for his $6 million man Milan Momcilovic , who promptly stepped out of bounds. Watch the play here: Milan Momcilovic steps out of bounds wow pic.twitter.com/SjqzMju5dN — wok (@wokdior) November 28, 2026 Kentucky actually did get one more chance to win the game after the illegal play on the baseline. Wichita State turned the ball over on the next possession, and Momcilovic got a decent look at a game-winning three, but missed. What this comes down to is poor execution by Kentucky, and it has Big Blue Nation ready to move on. Pope heard some boos from the home fans as he walked off the floor after the game: Mark Pope Boo’d out of Rupp Arena pic.twitter.com/C4n2tEvQ0z — Bleed Blue Network (@BleedBNetwork) November 28, 2026 Kentucky fell to No. 66 on KenPom after the loss . sports.title: Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in final practice for F1 Qatar GP
sports.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian Formula One driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes drives during the second practice of the Formula 1 2026 Qatar Grand Prix, at Lusail International Circuit. (is associated with: «Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in final practice for F1 Qatar GP») Alessio Morgese/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa World champion Kimi Antonelli led a third Mercedes one-two ahead of team-mate George Russell in the final practice for the Formula One Qatar Grand Prix on Saturday. The top two was a repetition of the previous two practice sessions on Friday. The Italian clocked the fastest time of 1 minute 22.400 seconds, beating Russell by 0.249 seconds. Max Verstappen of Red Bull was third ahead of team-mate Isack Hadjar. Charles Leclerc of Ferrari was fifth, with the McLaren duo of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri right behind in sixth and seventh respectively. Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton was ninth in the other Ferrari. The race in Qatar is taking place despite continuing security concerns due to conflicts in the Middle East. Several broadcasters and other personnel decided against attending the penultimate race of the season. Williams driver Carlos Sainz, who was 18th in practice, revealed on Thursday that drivers were briefed on emergency evacuation procedures and was surprised to discover journalists knew nothing about it. "I was told there was such a plan, and I expected the press would be included, too," he said. Qualifying for Sunday's showdown is later on Saturday. There's nothing more at stake at this point of the year, as Antonelli has already clinched the drivers' title and Mercedes have claimed the constructors' championship.

sports.description: Nations Championship Wales (26) 40 Tries: Adams 2, Murray, Morgan-Williams, Morgan 2 Cons: Costelow 5 Japan (0) 10 Tries: Komura, Vailea Wales finished their Nations Championship campaign with another victory against Japan in a six-try display at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. Wing Josh Adams and replacement flanker Jac Morgan claimed two tries apiece, with full-back Blair Murray and scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams also dotting down, while player of the match Sam Costelow kicked 10 points. This set up the most comprehensive margin of victory of the Steve Tandy coaching era in a match that was affected by the miserable conditions. Despite the scoreline, Wales again spent large periods of the game defending against a weakened Japan side who managed two late tries through replacements Shinya Komura and Halatoa Vailea. Returning flanker James Botham made 38 tackles as he equalled Dafydd Jenkins' world record effort in the 35-28 win against New Zealand, a mark they now both share with Thierry Dusautoir of France. It was a curious contest, low on quality, played in front of a half-empty Twickenham as part of a double-header before England faced New Zealand. The victory means Wales secured ninth in the inaugural Nations Championship and finished the year ninth in World Rugby's rankings. It was a second win in the space of three weeks against Japan, and a third victory in a November campaign that will forever be remembered for Wales beating New Zealand for the first time in 73 years. sports.title: Bucks add games against Jazz and Raptors to schedule
sports.description: Following the conclusion of preliminary NBA Cup play late on Nov. 27, the league added two regular-season games to the December schedule for teams that did not advance to the knockout rounds of the in-season tournament. The Milwaukee Bucks were one of those teams, and they had games against the Utah Jazz and Toronto Raptors added to their schedule. Milwaukee will head to Utah on Dec. 6 for a 4 p.m. CT game and host the Raptors on Dec. 10 at 7 p.m. CT. The Jazz game is an interesting addition, as the Bucks already had a trip to Salt Lake City on their schedule Jan. 26 as part of a West Coast trip. The game against the Raptors also will be the team's fourth meeting of the season and second at Fiserv Forum. The teams already have played twice, including the Bucks' second win of the season on Nov. 23. sports.title: Skip Bayless says Cowboys would’ve won vs Eagles if they had made the Dak Prescott trade he told them to
sports.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images Skip Bayless has continued to express his displeasure for Dak Prescott on the back of the Dallas Cowboys losing to the Philadelphia Eagles. The Cowboys are now 5-7 for the season after giving up 21 points against the Eagles, meaning there is a strong chance they will now go three years in a row without reaching the postseason. But rather than questioning Dallas’ defence, which is the worst in the league right now, Bayless has instead spoken of his desire to trade Dak Prescott for Jayden Daniels. Skip Bayless thinks Jayden Daniels would have helped the Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles Bayless already commented on his desire to trade Prescott for Daniels prior to the November trade deadline. Speaking in late October, he said: “If they want to trade me Jayden Daniels for Dak Prescott. It’s done. Straight up, player for player. Let me have him, I’ll take it. He was available all last year when we went 7-9-1. He’s been available this year; we’re 2-4. Give me Jayden Daniels.” Now, on the latest episode of Gridiron, Bayless has once again been speaking about trading for Daniels and this time claimed that the quarterback ‘gets that game home’ [against the Eagles]. He said: “If there’s some way that Washington would trade me Jayden Daniels straight up for Dak Prescott, which they would laugh at, I would do it in a heartbeat because I’ve got 25 years old versus 33, and I’ve got the clutch gene versus no clutch gene. That’s just me.” His fellow host replied: “Yeah, and you still would have lost 38-39 yesterday,” seeing Skip respond by suggesting Daniels would have won them the game. He said: “No, I would not have. Jayden Daniels gets that game home. He’s going to just keep on keeping on in the fourth quarter. He’s going to throw two more touchdown passes in the fourth quarter.” While Skip seems keen to move on from Prescott, Daniels’ stats have not been that impressive this season. He has 1,788 passing yards (3,340 for Dak), 10 passing touchdowns versus 27 for the Cowboys star and has a completion rate of 64.9% compared to 65.8% for Prescott. Bayless also mentioned Daniels having a ‘clutch gene’, which may be the only area he actually has the better of the Dallas QB. Prescott is 2-5 in postseason games throughout his career, while the Washington Commanders star is 2-1. sports.title: GB miss out on Davis Cup final as Alcaraz stars for Spain
sports.description: Great Britain were unable to give Leon Smith the perfect send-off as Davis Cup captain as Carlos Alcaraz inspired Spain to a 2-0 victory in the semi-finals. Competing in their first Davis Cup semi-final since 2019, Britain fell short as Arthur Fery was unable to match the dazzling brilliance of Alcaraz, with the seven-time major winner surging to an emphatic 6-2 6-1 win. That was after rising star Rafael Jodar defeated Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5 in the opening singles match to put Spain in the driving seat in Bologna. The defeat brings the curtain down on Smith's near 17-year tenure as captain, during which he led Britain to Davis Cup success in 2015. Spain captain David Ferrer, who is also stepping down after this year's tournament, will have the chance to guide his nation to their first Davis Cup title since 2019 when they face Italy in Sunday's final. Three-time defending champions Italy beat Spain in last year's final , although they are without talisman and world number two Jannik Sinner because of a wrist injury that will keep him out of the Australian Open. "It is a second straight final, it is going to be my first Davis Cup final, I'll do whatever it takes to win," said Alcaraz. "It's something I have been chasing for a really long time, to be in a Davis Cup final." Alcaraz back to brilliant best against Fery as Norrie loses After Norrie's defeat by Jodar, Fery was faced with the mammoth task of beating world number three Alcaraz - a player he had never faced before. Alcaraz lifted his first ATP Finals title six days earlier, a triumph that completed his astonishing return to the sport following four months out with a wrist injury. And his return to top form was on full display as he dismantled Fery, ranked 32nd, in a dominant first set in which he dropped just two points behind his first serve. Alcaraz's movement and shot-making continued to dazzle the crowd in Italy and Fery could do little to stop the Spaniard's sprint to the finish line. Alcaraz started the season by becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam with his Australian Open triumph, and now has the chance to end the year with his first Davis Cup title, one of the few trophies he has yet to win. For Fery, who enjoyed his career-best season and a fairytale run to the Wimbledon semi-finals, it was another harsh reminder of the gulf in class between himself and the game's top players after he fell in straight sets to world number one Alexander Zverev in Thursday's quarter-final. sports.title: F1 Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli completes practice clean sweep as Mercedes dominates
sports.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli has handed Mercedes a clean sweep of Qatar GP practice sessions as the Silver Arrows head to qualifying with a huge advantage. Russell went quickest before halfway as teams embarked on soft-tyre runs with Mercedes continuing its ominous form on the high-downforce motorcycle circuit of Lusail, only for Antonelli to take another chunk out of that laptime in the second half. Unlike Friday's twice red-flagged FP2 session, third practice took place without incident, which was partly thanks to a tepid start with little to no action early on. At the start, Pierre Gasly circulated by himself, making up for lost ground after beaching his Alpine in the gravel midway through Friday's second practice. Gasly was eventually joined by team-mate Franco Colapinto and Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, while the others stayed in the garage for the first third of the session. That all changed suddenly before the 20-minute mark as the heavy hitters embarked on soft-tyre runs - a compound projected to be only useful for qualifying. The race is expected to be completed on medium and hard Pirelli tyres, which are facing their most demanding weekend on the Lusail loop. As qualifying simulations got underway, outgoing world champion Lando Norris headed to the Turn 14 escape road after catching a violent snap of oversteer. As was the case during both of Friday's practice endeavours, Mercedes immediately took charge with George Russell's 1m22.983s leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli. That was over half a second better than what McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Max Verstappen could muster, the latter driving a Red Bull RB22 which required rebalancing after a tougher free practice outing. While Russell then drifted wide in Turn 5, Antonelli's second mid-session run yielded a time almost identical to his team-mate's, just 0.017s off. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes With 15 minutes to go, Verstappen briefly claimed top before Antonelli immediately retaliated and restored Mercedes' comfortable half-second cushion with a 1m22.400s effort. Russell had no answer for that flash of pace, conceding 0.249s. Verstappen remained third, a sobering 0.501s in arrears as the first non-Mercedes car, followed by team-mate Isack Hadjar. After a Friday which Charles Leclerc described as "very difficult", there was little progress for Ferrari as Leclerc took fifth, eight tenths behind Antonelli. McLaren also struggled more than was expected with sixth for Norris and seventh for Piastri. Lewis Hamilton fared worse after being held up by traffic on his final hotlap, splitting Racing Bull's midfield leaders Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson in ninth. technology.title: Quantum: 'Five years, that's all we got…'
technology.description: SC26 in Chicago had the usual quantum booths, discussions, and hallway optimism. A lot of people were talking about integration with classical HPC and Slurm scheduling for quantum processors, co-design platforms, and GPU-accelerated error correction tools. That part is real and useful. What was harder to find was any result that changed the basic math on when quantum systems will actually do something a supercomputer can't already handle better. I had a long conversation in St. Louis (SC25) with a contact who works deep in quantum and has spent decades in HPC. He's not a skeptic for sport, although that can be fun, sure. Over a grifted free dinner in Chicago (the best kind), his take this year remains the same: the hype keeps outrunning the error rates. Quantum computers generate too many errors to give usable answers on anything interesting. Fixing that is the whole game. And that's a five-year game, minimum. Much like the Bowie anthem in the title. Qubits by the numbers There are two kinds of qubits. Physical qubits are the actual hardware: ions, superconducting circuits, and atoms in a trap. Logical qubits are the ones that do the computation. Each logical qubit is built out of many physical ones so the system can detect and correct errors while it runs. With the traditional surface-code approach, one logical qubit often needs somewhere between 500 and 2,000 physical qubits backing it up, depending on the hardware and the code. One logical qubit by itself is useless. Estimates for basic scientific modeling and small-scale simulation sit in the 100-to-500 logical-qubit range. Take the midpoint of 300. At the low end of the overhead that is 150,000 physical qubits. At the high end it is several million. That is only for early science. Commercial work like molecular mapping for pharma, large optimization problems, complex financial models, pushes into the thousands of logical qubits. National-security and encryption-related work sits even higher. Those numbers have not magically shrunk. A system that can map a modestly sized drug molecule, or run a materials simulation that is still too slow on classical machines, is the kind of workload people actually mean when they talk about useful quantum advantage. Until the logical-qubit counts get there with error rates low enough to finish the job, those problems stay on the machines we already know how to build. Ok, so let's just scale it up This is the world of HPC, we know how to scale stuff, right? Yes, but this isn't a matter of adding a few more racks. Scaling to an additional few hundred thousand physical qubits is not a rack or two or ten. It's probably a dedicated building with its own cryogenics, control electronics, and power draw that is still measured in megawatts even before you get useful logical capacity. technology.title: Unkernel and Trynix just transported computing to 2035
technology.description: What's the difference between just-for-fun demo hacks, and serious carefully designed large-scale software architecture? It's the quick-and-dirty jobs that end up transforming computing. A blog post earlier this week called 2035 came early led the Reg FOSS desk down what we thought was a fascinating, and possibly quite scary, rabbit-hole… but it turned out to be an entire warren. We thought we were still in 2026, but in turns out that in some ways, tech just leaped forward a decade. To try to convey the point of this blog post – why what had been just a fun clever little hack has the potential to take half a century of OS and hypervisor design and throw it out of the nearest window – will take quite a lot of unpacking. If you bear with us, we will try to walk you through it. To get started, we need to go back a decade or more. Stick with this: there are laughs, as well as hammers taken to beloved ideas. The year of 2035 and the ideas around that come from a remarkable talk by Gary Bernhardt of Destroy All Software, which is both funny and highly educational. It will really massively assist understanding what this article and the technology is all about if you have the time to watch the talks. The Reg FOSS desk is not at all fond of spoken-word video as a medium – we much prefer to read than listen – but the three talks we're going to mention are golden, among the very best presentations this century in all of computing and IT. Seriously, they are worth your time. As a preface, before we go into Bernhardt's half-hour information-dense talk, let's warm up with a four-minute funny one. But first, let's look at the context for that. Step 0: JavaScript is the language of web programming In 2009, Jeff Atwood laid this out in an article called All Programming is Web Programming . It's still coming true today. Software is getting very blurred around the edges. The entire SaaS industry means that massive organizations run on web apps. Tech like Electron embeds a web browser inside JavaScript apps built in Node.js, while Progressive Web Apps make websites look like local program windows. The most popular desktop Linux in the world is ChromeOS Flex, which doesn't support local native applications at all. Everything is browser windows, even the desktop. It's all built in JavaScript. And yet… Step 1: JavaScript is kind of weird and kind of bad. Bernhardt made this case in 2012, with a celebrated lightning talk called Wat , from the CodeMash conference in 2012. Wat walks through a whole list of examples of how JavaScript is a very strange programming language and does very strange things that are not at all what you might expect. Some of the jokes will make more sense to programmers, but we reckon anyone who has ever fought with a recalcitrant bit of software will get some laughs from it – and that probably applies to all readers of The Register. Step 2: JavaScript is in the process of conquering the world. Bernhardt moved on to much bigger ideas at PyCon 2014

science.title: How moon dust and recycled cardboard could help NASA build its lunar base
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

The high cost of building on the moon has led to wide-ranging research on how to make use of the moon's most plentiful resource: the dusty regolith that covers its surface. Right now, lunar shipping runs about $544,000 per pound ($1.2 million per kilogram), so anything that astronauts can make on the moon using existing materials could help a lot. Scientists have already proposed using regolith for building 3D-printed bricks , solar arrays , and even as soil to grow potatoes . Now, a team of researchers from Purdue University in Indiana have developed an aerogel made from simulated regolith for insulating lunar habitats. New aerogels created by Purdue University researchers, made of cellulose and lunar regolith simulant, could pave the way for insulating materials made on the moon. (Image credit: Purdue University photo/John Underwood) "Sustaining a long-term presence on the moon will require us to rethink how we use local resources," Wei, professor in Purdue's James Tarpo Jr. and Margaret Tarpo Department of Chemistry, said in a Nov. 19 statement . NASA has said that it wants a long-term, sustainable moon base up and running by 2032, a goal it aims to achieve via its Artemis program . "Rather than relying on Earth to supply everything we need, we're exploring how materials already available on the moon, including waste generated by its inhabitants, could be upcycled into something essential for safe and livable habitats," Wei said. The aerogel that the Purdue researchers have been working on is a mix of fiber from cardboard waste, called cellulose, and a material that simulates regolith. They said that it could protect the people living in habitats from the moon's drastic temperature swings. "Imagine an aerogel as a high-tech thermos for a lunar base," Jacob Staker, a graduate researcher working on the study, said in the same statement. "Most of it consists of empty space that insulates the interior, helping it maintain the temperature of what's inside." The idea here is not to create the best aerogel possible, Wei said, but that "we're looking for the sweet spot where we can get the properties we need with the limited resources we have available" on the moon. The research was published in September in the journal ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 28, 1967: Astronomers Jocelyn Bell and Antony Hewish disover the 1st pulsar with Little Green Men 1 signal
science.description: null On November 28, 1967, astronomers found the first pulsar. A pulsar is a super-dense star that rotates super fast. As the pulsar spins, it emits two beams of light in opposite directions. When astronomers look at a pulsar, it looks like a star that's flickering on and off at a steady, constant pace. The first pulsar was observed by Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish. They were looking at the constellation Vulpecula when they saw a star flickering with regular pulses separated by 1.33 seconds. At first they had no idea what it was, so they jokingly nicknamed the signal Little Green Men 1. After more pulsars were discovered, they were able to rule out aliens. This chart tracked the signal of the first pulsar ever discoverered on Nov. 28, 1967. (Image credit: Cambridge University Library/Wikipedia) Why it mattered Pulsars are naturally occurring phenomena, and they can be handy tools for astronomers . For example, some pulsars are extremely accurate clocks. Because pulsars rotate, their emission of beams of radiation is observed at regular intervals. Until Burnell's discovery, astronomers did not know if neutron stars existed, let alone if they could be observed. "Suddenly, it turned out that nature has provided an incredibly precise way to observe these objects, something that has led to many later advances," said Edward Witten, chairman of the selection committee for the Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize, which in 2018 was awarded to Burnell . Among other applications, the observation of pulsars are one of the best ways astronomers have for testing Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity. The spinning stars have also been used as a navigation tool for spacecraft moving out beyond low Earth orbit. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .
